### ZWO

Registration: every ZWO device type is a catalog descriptor (`AlpacaCore/src/vendors/zwo/zwo_fields.h`, `zwo_schema.cpp`, `zwo_catalog.cpp`; open-astro#999); `router.cpp` holds no ZWO arm, include or sanitize branch. The telescope, filter wheel, focuser, rotator and switch factories are hardware-free `create` hooks. The camera is the one `Factory::bind` user (`bind_camera`): it receives the other stored ZWO camera entries (`BindContext::peers`, its own number included) and enumerates the SDK at registration, which `create` may not do. Its schema `normalize` owns the identity-string checks (control bytes, 64-digit hex serial) and "ZWO camera requires cameraIndex or cameraId"; `bind` owns the duplicate `serialNumber` refusal (a stored duplicate is cleared and relearned) and `claimed_serials`, and returns the learned `serialNumber` / `cameraName` for the router to store (#914). The camera's UniqueID is not ZWO's: the router serves the stored `uniqueId` of each configured device: a GUID it minted, or a kept `ZWO_UID_<hex>` ([decision 0018](../../docs/decisions/0018-persisted-unique-id.md), #1471). `register_zwo_camera_factory(catalog, sdk)` takes the SDK so `test_zwo_camera_catalog.cpp` runs it over `FakeZWOSDK`; a camera bind keeps going when the enumeration throws, so an unplugged camera still registers. All ZWO schemas set `forget_dropped_selectors`: a stored `*Index` / `*Id` that normalize drops, or that is not an integer, is removed and erased from the file so the entry still loads. The camera's selectors declare no range: `normalize_camera` checks -1 to INT_MAX itself to keep the arm's "expected an integer from -1 to 2147483647" text.

Devices: Camera, FilterWheel, Focuser (EAF), Rotator, Switch (dew heater, ASIAIR Pro / Plus Pi CM4 / Plus RK3568 12V power), Telescope (AM mount).

SDK locations: `AlpacaCore/external/ZWO/ASI_Camera_SDK/`, `EAF/`, `EFW/`, `CAA/`, `AM/`. The ASIair Pro switch driver does not use an SDK — it talks directly to the on-board Pi 4 GPIO via libgpiod v2.

EAF focuser `maxStep` (optional config): the unit clamps moves at its stored max step silently, so a driver-only limit (the QHY Q-Focuser shape) is not enough. At connect the driver writes `maxStep` with `EAFSetMaxStep` only when it differs from `EAFGetMaxStep` (never when unset, never when equal), clamps a value above `EAFStepRange` to it (one write of the clamped value, one WARN; an unavailable range is no bound), and still connects a stored 0 with nothing configured (WARN only; each `Move` is refused, as before the setting existed). The web UI input is blank-means-unset: do not give it a default.

EAF USB replug (#1500): the wrapper and `FakeZWOEAFSDK` compose `vendor::zwo::SharedOpenTable` (`shared_open_table.h`): an open returns a link and the serial read at the open, a second driver on the same unit shares it, and every per-device call runs under the caller's link (`with_link`; a call with no link is a `DriverException`, a retired link `NotConnected`). A different serial or a loss code behind a held id retires the entry and closes the dead handle at once. `EAF_ERROR_REMOVED`, `CLOSED`, BLE disconnect and `INVALID_ID` on a per-device call map to `NotConnected`, and one such error (the optional temperature read included) drops the link at once: `Connected` false, members `NotConnected`, one WARN with the escaped serial, last position and max step. One from the step range read fails the Connect, which closes what it opened. A generic error still counts toward the three-poll "communications compromised" latch. Once a serial is known (in memory, not persisted), every Connect scans the enumerated ids for it and never binds another unit; none found is `NotConnected` naming the recovery. A Disconnect whose close fails with `NotConnected` logs it and succeeds. Nothing is re-applied at relink beyond what every Connect does. The staleness bound (decision 0009 rule 2b) is not applied yet: the EAF stays on the 0009 `planned` row. Tests: the `[link]` cases in `test_zwo_focuser.cpp` and `test_zwo_shared_open_table.cpp`.

- ROI divisors: width%8, height%2 after binning (see [Camera ROI alignment](ascom-contract.instructions.md#camera-roi-alignment-all-camera-vendors)).
- Dew heater is exposed as an Alpaca Switch device (not a camera action) and is camera-dependent. It binds its camera by Auto, serial or index ([shared rule](ascom-contract.instructions.md#camera-attached-thermal-switches-pick-their-camera-zwo-touptek-player-one)); an index or serial binding lists the cameras, which opens every one because `ASIGetControlCaps` and `ASIGetSerialNumber` need an open camera; the legacy id-only binding (`cameraId` alone) opens only its own camera, and lists the others only to name them in a no-heater refusal.
- ST4 pulse guiding should be enabled only when the SDK reports `has_st4_port`.
- AM mount `:GMGE` / `:SMGE` longitude is west-positive; `SiteInfo`, ASCOM and persisted configuration are east-positive. Convert both reads and writes in the protocol wrapper only. Confirmed on AM5 USB during issue #1096 validation: reversing the wire sign brought the mount's `:GS` into agreement with GPS-based sidereal time; API site readback alone did not detect the mismatch.
- PulseGuide: do not apply permanent RA/Dec offsets based on expected guide motion. If synthetic offsets are needed, keep them temporary and clear after the pulse completes to avoid double-counting mount motion.
- The ZWO and QHY SDKs both statically link libusb, causing duplicate symbol issues. The ZWO vendor `CMakeLists.txt` handles this — do not link both vendor static libs into the same binary without resolving the conflict.
- **EAF, CAA, dew heater switch and AM mount follow the getters-never-wait order** ([decision 0016](../../docs/decisions/0016-getters-never-wait-on-device-io.md), #1392). Per driver:
  - **EAF, CAA and dew switch:** `transition_mutex_` spans `set_connected()`; the connect handshake and the close run under `io_mutex_`; `mutex_` is a short leaf never held across an SDK call. The status refill takes the cache mutex, then `io_mutex_`, so no code may call `status_cache_.reset()` or `invalidate()` while holding `io_mutex_` or `mutex_`. `fault()` is a leaf that takes only `fault_mutex_` and never waits on a refill, so a getter may call it. A refill that finds the driver disconnected (or, on the EAF, a lost link) returns a `closed` frame and the reader throws `NotConnected`: neither counts toward link health. `Name`, `MaxStep` and the names lists read values published at the end of connect; the `UniqueID` is the stored ID the router assigns at registration ([decision 0018](../../docs/decisions/0018-persisted-unique-id.md)), and only the fallback reads the serial from connect.
  - **AM mount:** `set_connected_mutex_` is the transition lock and the protocol wrapper's mutex is the I/O lock. `site_write_mutex_` serialises every site write (the setters and the connect's site apply, read-back and re-send) so a read-back never overwrites a setter; order `set_connected_mutex_`, `site_write_mutex_`, protocol mutex, `mutex_`. `guide_rate_writes_` makes the connect skip publishing its guide-rate reading when a `set_guide_rate()` landed meanwhile. `check_connected()` also requires `caches_ready_`, as `get_connected()` does; neither waits for readiness.
  - **EFW filter wheel (#1072):** same lock order as the EAF. `Position` is served from a 100 ms `util::TtlStatusCache` frame (one `EFWGetPosition` per refill, one per `DeviceState`); `-1` while moving comes through unchanged and is never held; `set_position` re-checks `connected_` under the I/O lock (a disconnect that won it has closed the wheel id) and invalidates the frame also when the move throws. Tests: the `[position-cache]` cases in `test_zwo_seam_fakes.cpp`.
  - The ASIAIR switches and the camera are not converted yet. Tests: the `[getter-stall]` cases in `test_zwo_focuser.cpp`, `test_zwo_rotator.cpp`, `test_zwo_switch.cpp` and `test_zwo_telescope.cpp` over the fake SDKs' delay knobs (`open_delay`, `read_delay`, `move_delay`; `*_delay_ms` on the dew fake) and `FakeZwoMount` (`AlpacaCore/tests/fake_zwo_mount.h`) for the AM mount, whose `hold_reply` and `delay_next` hold one exchange open in real time.
- ZWO camera SDK calls go through the injected `ZWOSDK` reference; its owner must outlive the driver, in-flight calls, and any delayed pulse-guide turn-off. `ASIGetDataAfterExp` is the lazy, potentially multi-second transfer: keep it outside the state and SDK-global locks, using only the per-camera operation lock that serializes transfer against start/close so abort and status calls remain responsive.
- A successful `ASIGetDataAfterExp` does not report the actual received byte count. Validate ROI/format readbacks and the converted array, but do not claim that a partially-written SDK buffer can be detected; retain fake coverage for transfer errors, not fabricated partial-length certainty.
- SDK 1.41 exposure-start USB reset evidence (#1665), recovered debug ABI and original-rig limits: [investigation](../../docs/zwo-exposure-resets.md). The OPi6/ASI6200 startup-reset trace is not evidence that the ASI2600/VIA-hub drop-off is fixed.
- **Acquisition metadata boundary** (issue #1477): SDK Success plus validated frame geometry publishes `LastExposure` before lazy transfer, whether reached through ImageReady or direct ImageArray. A later transfer failure retains that acquisition's metadata. Keep `acquisition_valid_` separate from published metadata, and refresh pending UTC/TaskClock start for each actual retry trigger after register reapplication. The UTC source is the host SDK invocation, not a measured sensor timestamp.
- Direct ImageArray during a retry re-trigger raises `InvalidOperation` until the new attempt is ready; a failed re-trigger reports its latched `DriverException` on the first read, not a supersession error.

#### ZWO AM telemetry (#1432, #1433)

- Each telescope owns its protocol wrapper, I/O mutex, handle and cancellation/loss state (#1524); disconnecting an idle entry must not close a sibling's link. Serial claims remain exclusive. Two explicitly configured TCP entries can still target one physical mount; use distinct endpoints. Multi-AM fake isolation coverage does not qualify two physical mounts.
- Auto discovery skips a sibling-held resolved IPv4 address and TCP port before opening a probe, logs at DEBUG and continues (#1536). Probes and final Auto opens atomically reserve the endpoint; explicit pairs retain their sharing policy. An explicit TCP open waits only for a discovery probe, up to one fixed 1500 ms steady-clock deadline (#1620); notifications never renew it. It rechecks ownership atomically and refuses an initializing or connected Auto link immediately. Wrapper cancellation is checked in at most 50 ms wait slices; public Disconnect keeps AsyncConnectable's deferred teardown semantics. The bound covers claim contention only, not DNS, TCP open or initialization. A link's reservation survives deferred close until its socket actually closes. The ZWO-local registry mutex is a leaf: no DNS, I/O, logging, callbacks, other locks or joins under it. `test_zwo_mount_network_isolation.cpp` uses per-wrapper candidate inputs and loopback servers; this is fake evidence, not a two-mount qualification.
- A fresh AM connection verifies its hash-terminated `:GVP#` model (AM3, AM5, AM5N or AM7) and fresh 12-hex `:GMA#` mount serial before enabling writes or publishing Connected (#1523); discovery uses the same model check, but never replaces the live connection's probe. Failed identity closes the link for explicit retry. A verified identity with unavailable initial telemetry may still connect. `:GMA#` evidence is in [Undocumented Serial Commands](../../AlpacaCore/external/ZWO/AM/Undocumented%20Serial%20Commands.md); this AM5 returned matching USB/handset Wi-Fi serials on firmware 1.8.6 and after its update to 1.8.8. Other units, model/firmware combinations and firmware transitions need their own rig evidence.
- `MountIdentityClaim` atomically reserves the fresh mount serial while initializing/connected; equal serials are refused when either entry uses Auto, including simultaneous connects. Release under the state lock on failed initialization, disconnect or link loss, with RAII as the destructor fallback. Its registry lock is a leaf under the state `mutex_` ([decision 0016](../../docs/decisions/0016-getters-never-wait-on-device-io.md) item 5) and never spans device I/O, other locks or joins. Two explicit entries retain the existing policy. This runtime serial is not persisted and never replaces the router-assigned ASCOM UniqueID; never use model, firmware, Bluetooth name or a cached reply as per-unit identity.
- AM reconnect identity (#1581): remember the first successfully claimed serial separately from active ownership, before enabling writes. Every later fresh connection must match, across link loss, explicit Disconnect and initialization failures after admission; malformed identity and refused duplicate claims learn nothing. The pin lasts for the driver object's lifetime, is not persisted and clears only on recreation: to admit a deliberate replacement, save the device again in the web UI (which removes and recreates the driver) or restart the service. Refuse a mismatch before configuration or motion writes, without printing either serial. Auto refuses a wrong selected unit rather than searching by serial ([decision 0009](../../docs/decisions/0009-link-loss-and-relink-policy.md)).
- The driver constructs its protocol wrapper with identity admission enabled. Until fresh verification and the identity claim finish, the wrapper admits only exact `:GVP#` and `:GMA#` response commands and no blind commands, checked under the I/O lock before discarding input or writing. Reconnect resets admission before opening the transport; an older caller cannot write through an unverified replacement link. Raw transport-only wrapper users retain their existing behavior.
- AlignmentMode, AtHome, Slewing, AtPark, Tracking, RA/Dec, Altitude/Azimuth and SideOfPier never do getter-originated I/O. They use `StateSnapshot<PolledFrame>` (SideOfPier derives hour angle from its RA and the cached site). A missing measurement raises `DriverException`, not a guessed value or `NotConnected` while Connected is true. TrackingRate is cached at connect/write; SiderealTime needs the cached site. UTCDate extrapolates a successful client/configured time write or mount reading using TaskClock elapsed time; an absent anchor raises `InvalidOperation`. When sync is disabled or fails and UTC is unset, connect samples `:GMTI` before publishing Connected; a redundant Connected=true also samples only if unset. The poll refreshes mount time every 30 s, never at getter time. Target RA/Dec, UTCDate and GuideRate getters require connection/readiness and link health, separately from their offline-capable setters. Both individual GuideRate setters write the shared rate through `set_guide_rate` without a getter pre-read, including through AlpacaHTTP; invalid values keep setter validation precedence.
- The snapshot freshness threshold is 5 s. Stale alone never refuses any of the telemetry getters above; health does. A mandatory sample is GU plus a complete RA/Dec pair. Moving GU can publish ahead of the pair, but cannot renew mandatory measurement age or clear a fault. Stopped status, GOTO completion and Park completion need the accepted pair. Optional horizontal/park replies do not restore health. A failed horizontal or fallback pier-side read clears that field, not mandatory health; its getters report unavailable until a successful measurement. AM5N stationary-implies-parked inference runs in the poll, not in AtPark or Slewing.
- Three consecutive failed mandatory polls latch a communications fault. Connected stays true; operational reads and ordinary writes raise `DriverException` with the single `get_link_fault()` text. A complete accepted mandatory sample restores service without reconnecting. AbortSlew and zero-rate MoveAxis still send stops while faulted; they remain `NotConnected` after loss.
- SiteLatitude and SiteLongitude reads use the same connection/readiness and health guard as GuideRate (#1681), including getter-triggered loss at the deadline; their offline-capable setters remain separate. IsPulseGuiding, Slewing shortcuts and rate reads already use that guard. The `[faulted-reads]` fake cases pin these paths, including a failed coordinate pair already in flight when a guide pauses later polls.
- AM5 can report `:Gps=2` (Park completed) without the `:GU` uppercase `N` stopped flag. Explicit Park completion wins after the startup guard and accepted mandatory pair; `Slewing` then respects the published parked state. Do not require `N` as well or Park never completes on this unit. The final-pair, forced-window and missing-`N` fake cases pin the boundaries.
- A fault standing for 30 s, a poll with no accepted mandatory sample for 30 s without a latch, or positive transport-loss evidence makes the link lost. An intentional pulse pause (including queued guides) defers the no-sample deadline until 30 s after its end, without renewing measurement age; a latched fault or transport loss still loses the link during the pause. Connected becomes false, DeviceState is empty, the snapshot is reset and transport close is best-effort outside the state lock. No automatic reconnect or motion replay. A timeout or parse failure alone is not transport-loss evidence. Skipped/paused polls count neither as failed exchanges nor measurements.
- All driver deadlines and waits use the injected TaskClock; UTC/LST values and protocol transport deadlines do not. The telemetry poll, the GOTO setup, the pulse drain and the disconnect teardown each run in an AsyncOperation slot ([decision 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-async-operation-ownership.md)); the poll is cancelled/joined outside the state lock before close. Every GOTO wire call goes through the send gate, and MoveAxis, FindHome, Park, AbortSlew, Sync and Unpark fence the GOTO (`fence_goto()`) instead of joining it. Pulse enqueue, `reset_position_offsets()` and connect reset take `pulse_mutex_` before the leaf state `mutex_`; loss cancellation cancels the pulse and GOTO slots under state (`cancel()` never blocks) and wakes the send gate only after releasing state.
- Connect resets health and the initial sample deadline before publishing the internally open link. Silence expiry applies only after warm-up; positive transport loss still aborts a handshake. A failed handshake clears its snapshot/health/loss text so offline configuration writes remain available; the async connection error retains the failure.
- Post-pulse coordinate reconciliation is best-effort and uses a 250 ms deadline per coordinate request (plus transport read granularity), not the configured multi-second link timeout: a missing response must not delay the next queued guide pulse. Every command discards already-pending serial/TCP input so a queued late reconciliation reply cannot become its response. A failed reconciliation does not renew measurement age; the mandatory poll remains responsible for health.
- Fake coverage: `test_zwo_telemetry_concurrency_stress.cpp` (unavailable cache, getter stalls, staged measurement age, mandatory failure/recovery/loss, transport removal, Park and fault/recovery lifecycle races), plus arrival/ownership cases in `test_zwo_async_slew_failure.cpp` and lifecycle storms in `test_zwo_concurrency_stress.cpp`.

#### ZWO ASIair Pro Switch (12V power ports via on-board GPIO)

End-user setup instructions live in [AlpacaCore/PowerPorts.md](../../AlpacaCore/PowerPorts.md); this section captures the implementation-side context.

- **Hardware reality**: ASIair Pro is a Raspberry Pi 4 (BCM2711) with a custom HAT exposing four 12V DC outputs. The stock ZWO firmware enables them at boot via `/boot/config.txt` under `[all]`: `gpio=18,12,13,26=op,dh,pu` (all four configured as output, default-high, pull-up). The boot-time `dh` flag is why all four DC ports come up powered as soon as the Pi boots — gear plugged in is "live" before any userspace runs.
- **Port-to-GPIO mapping** (Pi 4 ASIair Pro): Port 1 = GPIO 12, Port 2 = GPIO 13, Port 3 = GPIO 26, Port 4 = GPIO 18 on `/dev/gpiochip0`. Confirmed against the stock app via direct probe. Note: the order in `/boot/config.txt` (18,12,13,26) is *not* the port order.
- **Persistent state shape**: The stock ZWO `zwoair_imager` binary persists per-port settings in `~/.ZWO/ASIAIR_imager.xml` under the XPath `setting2/imager/gpio/port_N/` (zero-indexed: `port_0`..`port_3`). Each port has an `is_pwm` boolean flag. No per-port GPIO pin number is stored — the port-index→GPIO mapping is hard-coded in the stock binary. The device config carries `ports: [{gpio: N, pwm: bool}]`, but since #765 `configuredevice` refuses (HTTP 400, not saved) any `gpio` outside 12, 13, 26, 18 and any `gpioChip` other than `/dev/gpiochip0`, and the RK3568 variant any `devicePath` other than `/dev/pwm-gpio-misc`: a request must not choose which line or node the server opens. The same chip check applies to the iOptron iMate (`/dev/gpiochip1`, or the stock-BSP `/dev/gpiochip0`) and ToupTek StellaVita (`/dev/gpiochip0`) PowerBoxes.
- **App role abstraction is cosmetic**: the ASIair mobile app lets users assign a *role* to each port (Mount / Camera / Focuser / Dew Heater / Flat Panel / Other). Roles "Dew Heater" and "Flat Panel" enable software PWM dimming; the others are plain on/off. Under the hood every port can do either — the "role" is just a UI tag that sets the `is_pwm` flag. The AlpacaBridge driver does not model roles; it exposes 4 ASCOM Switch channels and lets users name them however they want.
- **PWM delta**: the stock app uses pigpio's DMA-based soft-PWM at 40 kHz; this driver uses the standard userspace soft-PWM ([general rules](ascom-contract.instructions.md#gpio-power-switch--soft-pwm-drivers-general-rules)) at a 1 kHz default — dew heaters don't care about frequency, and it stays portable off-BCM.
- **libgpiod v2** per the general rule; for older Bullseye/Bookworm hosts install libgpiod 2.x from backports rather than dual-targeting.
- **OS architecture gate**: AlpacaBridge is arm64-only. The factory stock ASIair Pro ships **32-bit Raspbian Buster armv7l** — our `.deb` will not install on the stock OS. Deployment requires re-imaging with Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit (Bookworm or Trixie). Once re-imaged, the stock `zwoair_imager` / `pigpiod` daemons must be disabled because they hold the GPIO lines via pigpio and would prevent libgpiod from claiming them (EBUSY on `gpiod_chip_request_lines`).
- **Boot default-on / disconnect**: general connect-reads-the-ports, power-on-state and never-power-cycle rules ([decision 0021](../../docs/decisions/0021-power-port-power-on-state.md)). On the rpt kernel `pinctrl_bcm2835 persist_gpio_outputs=Y` (checked 2026-10-25 on the CM4 rig, 6.18.50+rpt), so a released output keeps its level, low included. `powerOnState: off` turns the ports off at the first start of a boot; making them start off before AlpacaBridge runs is a `/boot/config.txt` `gpio=` change.
- **Coexistence with stock app is not supported**: libgpiod and pigpio cannot share GPIO line ownership. The stock `pigpiod` daemon (started by `/etc/rc.local → /home/pi/ASIAIR/asiair.sh`) must be disabled, and the stock `zwoair_imager` must not run. There is no way to run AlpacaBridge alongside the stock ASIair app on the same device.

#### ZWO ASIAIR Plus Switch (Pi CM4 variant — same libgpiod path as the Pro)

The CM4-based ASIAIR Plus is electrically a Pi-class board and **reuses the existing libgpiod `asiair` driver unchanged** — there is no separate CM4 driver, wrapper, or test file. It is surfaced only as a `switchType` alias in the catalog descriptor and the UI. Confirmed against live hardware on 2026-05-31 (host `astro.lan` / `192.168.1.171` — earlier notes said `asiair.lan`; the box was renamed, same device — stock firmware).

- **Hardware reality**: Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 (BCM2711). `/proc/device-tree/model` = "Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 Rev 1.0"; `/dev/gpiochip0` = `pinctrl-bcm2711` (58 lines) — the same bank the Pro driver targets. The board also carries a PCA9685 at I²C `0x40` and an `asiair-overlay` referencing `pwm-2chan` / MCP23017 / AXP209, **but none of those drive the four DC power ports** — they are red herrings (LED/PMIC/expander). The DC ports are plain BCM GPIO.
- **Port→GPIO mapping is IDENTICAL to the Pi 4 ASIAIR Pro**: Port 1 = GPIO 12, Port 2 = GPIO 13, Port 3 = GPIO 26, Port 4 = GPIO 18 on `/dev/gpiochip0`, active-high, default-on at boot. The stock `/boot/firmware/config.txt` directive is `gpio=12,13,18,26,5,6,16,17=op,dh` (the four DC ports plus four extra control lines 5/6/16/17 that the v1 driver ignores). So `default_asiair_pro_config()` is correct as-is for the CM4 Plus.
- **Mapping verified by "drive a known config, read it back"**: stock-app duty cycles matched `pigs gdc` exactly (59% → 590, 34% → 340). Gotcha: a single `pigs r <pin>` snapshot of a PWM pin races the duty cycle and often reads 0 — use `pigs gdc` or sample ~200× before concluding anything about a pin.
- **Reuse wiring**: the catalog accepts `switchType: "asiair-plus-picm4"` and routes it to `create_zwo_asiair_switch` / `default_asiair_pro_config()` with the same config sanitization as `asiair` (the `picm4` id was pre-reserved on the roadmap). Web UI adds an "ASIAIR Plus 12V Power Switch (Pi CM4)" dropdown option that reuses the Pro's per-port GPIO table. End-user setup lives in [AlpacaCore/PowerPorts.md](../../AlpacaCore/PowerPorts.md) under "ZWO ASIair Plus (Raspberry Pi CM4)".
- **Same OS / coexistence constraints as the Pro**: stock OS is 32-bit `armv7l` (kernel `5.10.27-v7l`) — requires re-imaging to arm64; the stock `pigpiod` / `zwoair_imager` must be disabled (libgpiod vs pigpio line-ownership conflict, `EBUSY`).
- **Model label (config-driven)**: the CM4 Plus reuses the Pro driver but reports the correct model. `AsiairSwitchConfig` carries a `model_name` (default `"ASIAIR Pro"`) that `get_name()`/`get_description()`/`get_driver_info()` interpolate; `zwo_catalog.cpp` sets it to `"ASIAIR Plus (Pi CM4)"` for `switchType: asiair-plus-picm4`. So the same driver serves both the Pro and the CM4 Plus, differing only by this label. ConformU 4.3.0 re-validated 2026-06-04 on the live CM4 (host `astro.lan`, `192.168.1.171`) — 0 errors / 0 issues / 0 timing, reporting "ASIAIR Plus (Pi CM4)".
- **Branding**: user-facing strings were normalized "ASIair" → **"ASIAIR"** (ZWO's actual product branding) across both switch drivers, the Web UI, and tests. Internal `switchType` ids (`asiair`, `asiair-plus-picm4`, `asiair-plus-rk3568`), log categories, and the gpiod consumer label stay lowercase/unchanged.

#### ZWO ASIair Plus Switch (RK3568 variant — kernel module ioctl, not libgpiod)

- **Hardware reality**: ASIair Plus (RK3568) is a Rockchip RK3568 SoC with a custom ZWO HAT. The four 12V DC outputs are **not** standard Linux GPIO from the user-space side — ZWO ships a custom kernel module (`pwm_gpio.ko`, author "JerryCui") that owns the device-tree `airplus-gpios` node and registers a misc-device character node at `/dev/pwm-gpio-misc` (major 10, minor 55). All port control goes through documented ioctls on that fd. This means standard `libgpiod` / `gpioget` tools see the lines as already-claimed and cannot drive them.
- **Reverse-engineered ioctl header**: first-party, at `AlpacaCore/src/vendors/zwo/pwm_gpio.h` (scanned by CodeQL, unlike `external/`). Source: decoded from DWARF debug info on the production ZWO kernel module. Defines `gpio_level_t`, `pwm_param_t`, `work_mode_t` plus the ioctl numbers (`PWM_GPIO_SET_LEVEL`, `PWM_GPIO_SET_MODE`, `PWM_GPIO_SET_CONFIG`, etc.). Treat this header as the canonical interface contract — do **not** invent new ioctls without confirming against the module disassembly.
- **Port index mapping (kernel module side)**: indices 0..11. Indices 0, 1 = LEDs; 2 = physical button (input); **3 = "DC master enable / control signal"** (must be HIGH for the DC ports to deliver voltage); **4..7 = the four DC power ports (PWM-capable)**; 8..11 = USB2/USB3 power enables. The AlpacaBridge driver exposes only indices 4..7 as wrapper indices 0..3 — USB power and button are deliberately out of scope for the v1 Switch driver to keep the ASCOM contract focused. Document any future extension here.
- **open() is read-only — do NOT touch any kernel-side state on connect.** Two earlier attempts to "initialize" the kernel module from open() — first driving the master-enable line at kernel index 3, then explicitly setting mode + level on each DC port — both produced the same symptom: every DC port physically dropped to 0 V the moment an ASCOM client connected. The kernel module is closed-source / reverse-engineered. `open()` opens the fd and does nothing else. The constructor's optimistic cache (value=1 / 100 = "on") is left in place — matches typical boot-time behavior of all four DC ports being live. The first hardware write happens when an ASCOM client calls `SetSwitch` or `SetSwitchValue`, or at server start when `powerOnState` is `restore` or `off` ([decision 0021](../../docs/decisions/0021-power-port-power-on-state.md)), through the same `set_value()` path. Do not add any write to `open()` or to connect.

- **PWM_GPIO_GET_LEVEL lies.** Empirically (probed across all 12 kernel indices on a freshly-booted device with all DC ports physically powered and the network LED lit): `GET_LEVEL` returns 0 for every index. It reads the kernel module's "last-written via SET_LEVEL" cache, which initializes to 0 at module load regardless of what pinctrl drove the pads to physically. So **never** trust `GET_LEVEL` for state introspection — the UI will silently flip to "all off" on first connect after fresh boot, even though every port is hot. Read `/sys/kernel/debug/gpio` (line directions and levels) for true state when debugging.

- **The kernel module needs SET_MODE → ENABLE → SET_LEVEL.** Reverse-engineered the hard way after observing that toggles in NINA had zero physical effect even though every ioctl returned 0. The kernel debug interface revealed the DC port GPIO lines (GPIO 146/147/149/150 on gpiochip4) were stuck as **inputs** with external pull-ups holding them HIGH, regardless of how many `SET_LEVEL` calls our driver made. The kernel module silently rejects writes to lines that aren't in OUTPUT direction (it logs `"NOT in GPIO OUTPUT mode"` via printk but returns 0 to userspace). The fix: call `PWM_GPIO_ENABLE` between `SET_MODE` and `SET_LEVEL` — internally that maps to `gpiod_direction_output_raw` and flips the line.

- **SET_LEVEL polarity is INVERTED from typical gpiod semantics.** Verified by reading `/sys/kernel/debug/gpio` after each ioctl AND physically observing a 12V flat panel on DC port 2: `SET_LEVEL(0)` resolves the line to `in hi` (input, pulled high externally) which **powers the panel ON**; `SET_LEVEL(1)` resolves to `out lo` (output driven low) which **cuts power**. So in the wrapper, ASCOM `value=1` (on) maps to ioctl `level=0`, and `value=0` (off) maps to ioctl `level=1`. This is non-standard — typical gpiod chips treat `level=1` as drive-high — and the cause is almost certainly a quirk in the closed pwm_gpio.ko's level-argument interpretation (likely `level=1` maps internally to `gpiod_direction_output_raw(0)` while `level=0` maps to `gpiod_direction_input`, judging by the kernel debug state transitions). Don't "fix" this by flipping it back — the previous polarity produced the inverted-feeling NINA behavior the user reported on 2026-05-30 ("when I flip it on it goes off") and connected gear lost power on every value-set transition.

- **The kernel module's PWM mode is unreachable from documented ioctls — we do userspace soft-PWM instead.** SET_MODE(PWM) → ENABLE → SET_CONFIG returns success on every input (GET_CONFIG echoes back the period/duty we wrote), but the kernel's hrtimer dispatch branch never actually arms — `/proc/timer_list` shows no `pwm_gpio_timer_func` scheduled regardless of ordering, period, or duty. Disassembly of `pwm_gpio_misc_ioctl` shows the `hrtimer_init` + `hrtimer_start_range_ns` call sites do exist at file offset 0x7c0–0x7ec inside the misc-ioctl dispatcher, but they're gated by a condition we cannot trigger from userspace. The closed source means we can't confirm the gate definitively (the inventory's "GPL" license claim notwithstanding — try ZWO support if source-level fixes are ever needed). The DTS also confirms there's no hardware PWM controller mapped to the airplus-gpios pins on GPIO bank 4, so even if we triggered the hrtimer branch we wouldn't get hardware PWM — just kernel-side soft-PWM. So we run the standard userspace soft-PWM ([general rules](ascom-contract.instructions.md#gpio-power-switch--soft-pwm-drivers-general-rules)) over `SET_LEVEL`, with this module's inverted polarity. Confirmed against the extracted stock `zwoair_imager` daemon (`pwm_gpio_start` symbols — same approach). Default 50 Hz = the stock daemon's actual `period_ns = 20,000,000`, read back live via `PWM_GPIO_GET_CONFIG` (see the comment in `default_asiair_plus_rk3568_config`); range 1–100,000 Hz via `pwmFrequencyHz`.

- **Module forensics one-liners**: license GPL, author `JerryCui` — source must be obtainable from ZWO if kernel-side fixes are ever needed. Runtime introspection: `cat /sys/kernel/debug/gpio` (true line directions/levels), `/sys/firmware/devicetree/base/pinctrl/airplus_gpios/airplus-ports` (pin map).
- **Disconnect**: general never-power-cycle rule — the kernel module retains per-port mode + level across opens, so releasing our fd power-cycles nothing.
- **Index 3 is unresolved**: the bullet above calls kernel index 3 the "DC master enable", but the RK3568 device tree and the clean-room `pwm_gpio_compat` module both put the piezo buzzer (gpio0/15) there and show no master-enable line. Nothing in the driver touches index 3; confirm on hardware before relying on either reading.
- **Permissions**: `/dev/pwm-gpio-misc` is created with root-only mode by the kernel module. We ship a udev rule (`AlpacaCore/external/ZWO/asiair-plus/99-zwo-asiair-plus.rules`) that grants the `gpio` group `0660` access. `build_and_run.sh` and the `.deb` postinst both install it via the existing rules-discovery loop in `external/`. The AlpacaBridge daemon user (and any human user wanting to poke at the device) must be in the `gpio` group.
- **Kernel module hard dependency**: `pwm_gpio.ko` ships only with ZWO's stock kernel build (4.19.219). Re-flashes that swap to mainline RK3568 distros (Armbian, etc.) will **not** include it, and the driver will fail to open `/dev/pwm-gpio-misc`. The flashing tool tracked at `rk-flashtool` is the supported path; document any alternatives here as they emerge.
- **Config schema** (`zwo_fields.h`, `switchType: "asiair-plus-rk3568"`): much simpler than the Pro because the kernel module fixes the index mapping. Fields are `devicePath` (default `/dev/pwm-gpio-misc`), `pwmFrequencyHz`, and a `ports[]` array where each entry is just `{ name, pwm }`. No `gpio` / `gpioChip` fields — they would be meaningless for this hardware.
- **Web UI naming convention**: device label is "ASIair Plus 12V Power Switch (RK3568)" — explicit because a Pi-CM4 variant (`asiair-plus-picm4`) is on the roadmap. Do not collapse the two to a bare `asiair-plus` `switchType`; the kernel-interface difference between the CM4 (libgpiod, like the Pro) and the RK3568 (kernel module, like this driver) is fundamental.
